root_idea.summary: The root centers on the opposite of prosperity or good fortune: adverse fortune, misfortune, and ill omen.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from adverse fortune to adverse days, and to نُحَاس for copper or brass and for smoke or fiery emissions. A color association between a reddening horizon or flame and copper is offered as an explanatory development, not as a universal direct meaning of every form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested noun meaning misfortune or an adverse day.
Distinct Quran-attested noun with competing smoke, fiery-emission, and copper interpretations.
Distinct Quran-attested plural adjective, normalized to the singular citation form نَحِس.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence it appears in the construction “a day of misfortune.” The noun denotes adverse fortune generally; an alternative adjectival reading of the cited expression is also reported, while the QAC form represented here is the noun.

senses.definition: Smoke or a smoke-like heated emission.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passage, it is understood as smoke; explanations differ over whether the emission has flame, rises high, or is associated with molten metal.

senses.definition: A flame or fiery blaze without smoke.
senses.usage_conditions: An interpretation of the Quranic passage understands نُحَاس as a smokeless flame, with the term associated by color with copper.

senses.definition: Copper, brass, or molten copper-like metal.
senses.usage_conditions: Some Quran-focused interpretations of the passage understand نُحَاس as copper or brass itself, including molten metal.

The Quranic form is the plural feminine adjective describing days as adverse or ill-omened. One reported interpretation understands the days as severely cold; this is an explanatory interpretation of the same Quranic construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become unprosperous, unfortunate, inauspicious, or unlucky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person, a star, or another thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a fire, to give off much smoke.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV verbal use describing the production of abundant smoke.
Also used of a person's fortune when it is overturned or ruined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulty, distress, trouble, fatigue, harm, injury, or an evil condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader noun branch distinct from the Quranic construction meaning an adverse day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a year, marked by dearth, drought, or sterility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of a barren or unproductive year.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pair of planets Saturn and Mars.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional dual appellation for these two planets.
The material term may include a strongly red copper or brass substance and molten copper.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fire, or sparks produced when brass or iron is struck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the fiery sparks or discharge produced by striking the metal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nature, natural disposition, quality, or origin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's character or of the origin from which a thing derives.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coppersmith or worker in copper or brass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun formed from the material term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of misfortune, unluckiness, or adverse fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting a location characterized by ill luck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of misfortune, unluckiness, or adverse fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting something that brings about ill luck.

cautions: نُحَاس in 55:35 has competing Quran-focused interpretations, including smoke, a smokeless flame, and copper or molten copper; these are preserved as distinct senses rather than collapsed into the contextual English gloss.
For 54:19, the QAC form is the noun نَحْس, although an adjectival reading of the expression is also reported.
A variant reading نَحَسَات is reported for 41:16; the form accounted for here is the QAC adjective نَحِسَات.
